props.title: The Returned

sections.content: **Les Revenants/The Returned** (2004) revolutionized zombie cinema by stripping away horror conventions for raw emotional impact. Unlike George Romero's **Night of the Living Dead** (1968) or Danny Boyle's **28 Days Later** (2002), director Robin Campillo presents the dead simply walking home, creating an eerie meditation on grief and acceptance. The film's influence echoes through later works like **The Leftovers** (2014) and **Maggie** (2015), establishing a new subgenre of contemplative undead stories.

sections.content: Campillo's film sparked a wave of European horror that prioritized emotional resonance over scares. **A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night** (2014) and **Raw** (2016) continued this tradition, using genre elements to explore complex human relationships. The French series adaptation of **Les Revenants** (2012) expanded the concept further, diving deeper into community dynamics when facing the impossible. SUBHEAD: Reinventing Undead Cinema

The Returned's influence extends beyond horror into arthouse territory. Films like **Only Lovers Left Alive** (2013) and **Personal Shopper** (2016) adopted its measured pace and focus on existential themes. This approach transformed supernatural elements into metaphors for loss, memory, and cultural identity.
